title: Efficient ELISA for SARS-CoV-2 Spike-Specific IgG Measurement
author: Appeltrath, Parreuter, et al.

steps.title: Prepare safety and work conditions
steps.instruction: Wear required personal protective equipment and follow all applicable safety regulations. Perform the ELISA at room temperature, do not shake the plate, and seal the plate with a plate sealer during all incubation periods. Use a multichannel pipette and a reservoir whenever possible, and prepare sample dilutions in cell‑culture plates rather than 1.5 mL reaction vessels.

steps.title: Coat plates with SARS‑CoV‑2 spike (initial test)
steps.instruction: Prepare a coating solution of soluble SARS‑CoV‑2 spike at 10 µg mL⁻¹ in coating buffer and add to the wells. Incubate at room temperature, seal the plate, and do not shake.

steps.title: Optimize coating concentration
steps.instruction: Perform a titration using spike concentrations ranging from 0.3 µg mL⁻¹ to 10 µg mL⁻¹ with a sample dilution of 1:100. Identify 5 µg mL⁻¹ as sufficient to detect highly reactive samples without signal loss and adopt this concentration for the final protocol.

steps.title: Prepare sample dilutions (optimization)
steps.instruction: Create serial dilutions of human plasma/serum: test 1:80, 1:100, and 1:200 dilutions (the latter giving the highest resolution). For routine assays, use a 1:200 dilution prepared in cell‑culture plates.

steps.title: Add diluted samples to coated wells
steps.instruction: Dispense the prepared sample dilutions into the spike‑coated wells. Seal the plate and incubate at room temperature without shaking (incubation time not specified in the source).

steps.title: Optimize detection‑antibody dilution
steps.instruction: Test detection‑antibody dilutions of 1:5,000, 1:10,000, 1:20,000, and 1:40,000. Observe that 1:5,000 and 1:10,000 give signals above the plate‑reader detection limit, 1:40,000 yields poor resolution, and 1:20,000 provides optimal signal‑to‑noise. Adopt a 1:20,000 dilution for the final protocol.

steps.title: Add detection antibody
steps.instruction: Add the detection antibody diluted 1:20,000 to each well. Seal the plate and incubate at room temperature without shaking (incubation time not specified).

steps.title: Optimize development time
steps.instruction: Evaluate substrate development times of 10 min, 20 min, and 30 min. Select 30 min as the optimal development time for the best signal‑to‑noise ratio.

steps.title: Develop signal
steps.instruction: Add the appropriate substrate (type not specified) and develop the reaction for 30 minutes at room temperature, sealing the plate and avoiding shaking.
